correctness.rationale:
For any even k>=2, rho(k) is the least prime not dividing k. For any prime p>B(k)>=rho(k), p is odd and p≠rho. Since k is invertible mod rho, one of p,p+k,...,p+(rho-1)k is divisible by rho; the first such positive-index composite occurs by ell<=rho-1. As k even, c=p+ell*k is odd composite, hence P^+(c)<=c/3<= (p+k(rho-1))/3

k(rho-1)/2. A periodic orbit contains a prime; if all its primes exceeded B, consecutive prime-block transitions would strictly descend, contradicting cyclicity. Distinct orbits are disjoint and inject into primes<=B, giving L(k)<=pi(B). For even k>=4 with 3∤k, rho=3 and B=k; for 6|k,5∤k, rho=5 and B=2k; k=2 B=3. Git-blob-verified verify.py replay returned VERIFY_OK for finite ranges, but symbolic proof establishes all even k.
residual_risks: The argument is conditional on the precise prime/composite definition for all states>=2 and rho(k) being a prime.
Finite tests do not prove all-k arithmetic; proof uses modular divisibility and 1/3 odd-composite inequality.

value.rationale: This provides a start-independent, parameter-explicit localization of every periodic orbit for a natural arithmetic dynamical map and bounds the number of cycles. For the infinite congruence family of even k>=8 with 3∤k it replaces Das’s k sqrt(k)/2 prime-locator scale with the linear bound B=k; for 6|k,5∤k it gives the similarly explicit B=2k. The mathematical reason is a structural parity-specific 1/3 contraction after a prime-run bounded by rho(k), not a finite empirical gain or renaming. This is useful for exact searches and for the open study of cycle growth; it does not determine L(k) exactly or solve its unboundedness.
residual_risks: Not optimal for every small even parameter; no claim of sharpness or exact cycle enumeration.
An elementary synthesis may have limited independent methodological novelty even though quantitative family-wide improvement is mathematically motivated.
